marks.gloss_en: אלמא -- since the buyer of the innards gives the gifts without deducting, a person does not sell the priest's gifts
הכא נמי מתנות דכהן לא מזבין איניש
הלכך: שייר המוכר -- מוכר חייב, דאמר ליה לוקח: מתנה דכהן גבך היא
לא שייר -- לוקח חייב, דאמר ליה מוכר: מתנה דכהן לא זבני לך
evidently, a person does not sell the priest's gifts
פשיטא! משום דאיקדש פקע ליה איסור גיד הנשה מיניה? -- consecration cannot abrogate the nerve's ban, so 'and in consecrated animals' teaches nothing there
wherever we learned 'with non-sacred and with consecrated animals' it is stated needfully
סלקא דעתך אמינא: הואיל ובעניינא דקדשים כתיב -- one might have reasoned from its being written among the laws of sacrifices
wherever we learned 'in the presence of the Temple and not in its presence' it is stated needlessly
ולאו אוקימנא בוולדות קדשים? -- did we not establish the nerve's mishna as dealing with offspring of consecrated animals? then its phrase is needed

ומאי טעמא אוקימנא? לאו משום דקשיא לן לא ליתני? מעיקרא נמי לא תקשי לך: איידי דתנא לצורך, תנא נמי שלא לצורך -- the okimta was forced only by the difficulty 'let it not teach it'; since the phrase was taught needfully, it was taught needlessly too, and the difficulty never arises
wherever we learned 'in the Land and outside the Land' it is stated needlessly
הלכך -- the derasha that excludes the consecrated bird (138b.10) excludes, therefore, the bird that killed a person
מאי טעמא? דאמר קרא שלח תשלח את האם -- one you are commanded to send, excluding one you must bring to court
Ravina: therefore a kosher bird that killed a person is exempt from sending away
'you shall surely send the mother' -- one you are commanded to send away, excluding this one, which you are commanded not to send but to bring to the treasurer
sending the nest applies in the Land and outside the Land
what is not readily available? such as geese and chickens that nested in the orchard
